record.rationale: Complete Self Part B Amendment 1 deletes proposed section 307, not the whole H.R.3383 package. The retained December 2 RCP119-15 cover and complete section 307 bind the target: SEC rules requiring specified multi-class-share ownership and voting-power disclosures in proxy/consent material or another appropriate filing, covering directors, nominees, named executives and specified five-percent voting-power holders. It does not abolish multi-class shares, change voting rights or establish repeal of all existing Exchange Act disclosure rules. The whole exact child concerns securities governance and financial disclosure without a direct infrastructure or technology mechanism. Its 54–374 rejection with eleven Not Voting did not delete the section. No investor outcome, individual eligibility, voting recommendation, motive or current-law result is inferred.

record.rationale: Complete Waters Part B Amendment 3, offered as Garcia of Texas’s designee, adds a Title IV Treasury-rule requirement for investment advisers and defined hedge funds to comply with know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering requirements for foreign clients to the same extent as financial institutions under the specified Bank Secrecy Act subchapter. It does not itself ban foreign clients, deem them unlawful or prove a particular entity’s misconduct. The hedge-fund definition uses the specified Investment Company Act exclusions. Whole material financial-institution, adviser, fund, client and recordkeeping/implementation baselines and the financial-compliance versus direct technical-governance boundary remain pending. Its 211–219 rejection with eight Not Voting is distinct from parent passage; no enacted compliance change, prevented crime, privacy outcome or motive is inferred.
